parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Outline what is meant by a travelling wave.

answer.text:
Official markscheme checked; editorial worked explanation:

A travelling wave is a disturbance in which oscillations of a medium or field propagate through space, transferring energy, momentum or information. Features such as crests and troughs move with the wave.

evidence.detail: May 2024 SL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6711M, PDF page 7, checked against this exact subpart.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: The sound frequency is 210 Hz. Calculate the speed of sound in the pipe, stating the answer to an appropriate number of significant figures.

answer.text:
Official markscheme checked; editorial worked explanation:

Using v = fλ, v = 210 × 1.60 = 336 m s⁻¹. This is 3.36 × 10² m s⁻¹, or about 3.4 × 10² m s⁻¹ if reported to two significant figures; the official markscheme accepts either two or three significant figures.

evidence.detail: May 2024 SL Paper 2 TZ2 markscheme 2224-6711M, PDF page 7, checked against this exact subpart.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Which statement correctly describes a progressive longitudinal mechanical wave?

A. Energy transfer is perpendicular to particle oscillations; no medium is required.
B. Energy transfer is perpendicular to particle oscillations; its speed is always the same.
C. Energy transfer is parallel to particle oscillations; no medium is required.
D. Energy transfer is parallel to particle oscillations; it requires a medium and its speed depends on that medium.

answer.text: D. Longitudinal particle oscillations are parallel to propagation. A mechanical wave needs a medium, and its speed is determined by the medium’s properties.

parts.display_text:
The diagram is a displacement–position snapshot of a travelling wave. One wavelength corresponds to a phase change of 360°. What phase change accumulates from P to Q along the positive horizontal direction?

A. 180°
B. 450°
C. 540°
D. 720°

answer.text: B. P to Q spans one complete wavelength plus a quarter wavelength: 1.25 × 360° = 450°, equivalent to 90° modulo a complete cycle.

A. 0.28I
B. 0.53I
C. 1.9I
D. 3.5I

answer.text: D. The amplitudes are approximately 0.40 cm and 0.75 cm. I_Y/I_X = (0.75/0.40)² ≈ 3.5.

A radio pulse travels from Earth to Jupiter, reflects, and returns to Earth after 3960 s. Treat the separation as constant during the measurement and use radio-wave speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What distance between the reflecting surfaces does this imply?

A. 5.94 × 10⁸ km
B. 1.19 × 10⁹ km
C. 5.94 × 10¹¹ km
D. 1.19 × 10¹² km

answer.text: A. The one-way distance is ct/2 = (3.00 × 10⁸)(3960)/2 = 5.94 × 10¹¹ m = 5.94 × 10⁸ km.

answer.text: X-rays. A wavelength of 21 pm is 2.1 × 10⁻¹¹ m, in the short-wavelength X-ray region for radiation generated by electron processes at a target.

Which approximate free-space wavelength range corresponds to infrared radiation?

A. 100 nm to 400 nm
B. 300 μm to 30 cm
C. 400 nm to 700 nm
D. 800 nm to 1000 μm

answer.text: D. Infrared lies beyond the red end of visible light and extends towards roughly 1 mm. 800 nm to 1000 μm (1 mm) is the appropriate approximate range.

parts.display_text:
A progressive wave has frequency 300 Hz and speed 600 m s⁻¹. Two points along its propagation direction are 0.50 m apart. Use the fact that one wavelength corresponds to 360° of phase. What is their phase difference?

A. 45°
B. 90°
C. 180°
D. 360°

answer.text: B. λ = v/f = 600/300 = 2.0 m. The separation is 0.50/2.0 = 1/4 wavelength, so the phase difference is 90°.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Use the supplied wave relations: intensity I is proportional to amplitude², and power reaching a perpendicular surface is P = IS, where S is its area. A plane wave of amplitude A delivers power E to area S. Its amplitude becomes 2A and the area becomes S/2. What power reaches the smaller surface?

A. 4E
B. 2E
C. E
D. E/2

answer.text:
Official key B checked; editorial worked explanation:

B. Doubling amplitude multiplies intensity by 2² = 4. Halving the surface area multiplies intercepted power by 1/2. Therefore P′/P = 4 × 1/2 = 2, so the new power is 2E.

parts.display_text:
An electromagnetic wave travels through vacuum. Which wavelength-period pair is possible?

A. 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁰ Tm and 2.5 Ms
B. 1.2 pm and 2.5 × 10¹¹ Gs
C. 1.2 × 10² pm and 4.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ ns
D. 1.2 × 10³ μm and 4.0 ns

answer.text:
Official key C checked; editorial worked explanation:

C. Convert option C: λ = 1.2 × 10² pm = 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁰ m and T = 4.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ ns = 4.0 × 10⁻¹⁹ s. Then λ/T = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, the speed of light in vacuum.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A transverse wave travels from left to right on a string. At the shown instant, points 1 and 3 lie on rising spatial slopes and point 2 lies on a falling slope. Which option gives their velocity directions?

A. right, right, right
B. right, left, right
C. up, down, up
D. down, up, down

answer.text:
Official key D checked; editorial worked explanation:

D. Imagine the entire profile shifted a little to the right. At the fixed positions of points 1 and 3, the shifted profile is lower, so those particles move down. At point 2 the shifted profile is higher, so that particle moves up. The directions are therefore down, up, down.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A guitar string is plucked. Which statement describes the resulting waves?

A. Longitudinal on string, longitudinal in air
B. Longitudinal on string, transverse in air
C. Transverse on string, longitudinal in air
D. Transverse on string, transverse in air

answer.text:
Official key C checked; editorial worked explanation:

C. Elements of the string move perpendicular to wave travel, so the string wave is transverse. Sound in air consists of pressure compressions and rarefactions parallel to propagation, so it is longitudinal.

evidence.detail: Cambridge 9702/12 May/June 2024 published key C, PDF page 2; explanation is editorial.

parts.display_text: At t=0 the source snapshot shows two fixed water particles P and Q at different positions along one progressive wave. Which source graph gives their phase difference φ as time passes?

answer.text:
Published key D checked; editorial worked explanation:

D. For a progressive wave of fixed wavelength, the phase difference between two fixed positions depends on their constant separation along the wave. Both particles continue oscillating at the same frequency, so their phase lag remains constant in time. The nonzero horizontal line is D.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
What is the approximate frequency range of electromagnetic radiation visible to the human eye?

A. 430–750 kHz  B. 430–750 MHz  C. 430–750 GHz  D. 430–750 THz

answer.text:
Published key D checked; editorial worked explanation:

D. Visible wavelengths are roughly 400–700 nm. Since f=c/λ, these correspond to frequencies of order 4×10¹⁴ to 8×10¹⁴ Hz, or hundreds of terahertz. Thus 430–750 THz is the appropriate range.

evidence.detail: Cambridge 9702/12 February/March 2023 published key D, PDF page 2; explanation independently authored and checked.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Explain how air-molecule motion creates compressions and rarefactions in a longitudinal sound wave.

answer.text: Official markscheme points: molecules oscillate parallel to propagation and create alternating high- and low-pressure regions. Editorial worked explanation: Air molecules move back and forth about equilibrium along the direction the wave carries energy. Where neighboring molecules crowd together, density and pressure rise to form a compression; where they spread apart, density and pressure fall to form a rarefaction.
answer.evidence: OCR H156/01 June 2023 markscheme checked on PDF page 12; editorial explanation independently recalculated.

parts.display_text: A transverse wave travels right at 8.0 m s⁻¹. The source figure marks successive horizontal grid intervals as 0.10 m. (a) Read the wavelength from the figure and calculate the frequency. (c) If the source frequency increases, explain what happens to wavelength and state an assumption.

answer.text: Official report checked; editorial worked explanation: one wavelength spans four 0.10 m intervals, so λ=0.40 m and f=v/λ=20 Hz. Assuming unchanged string tension and linear density, speed remains constant; λ=v/f therefore decreases.

answer.text: Editorial correction to the official report: Δx=vΔt=8.0(0.025)=0.20 m, two 0.10 m segments and half a wavelength. Draw the unchanged profile shifted two segments right. The report prints 0.02 m but its conclusion and answer figure show 0.20 m. Assume constant propagation speed and negligible damping and dispersion, so the wave shape and amplitude are unchanged.
